literal: By deceit wealth having acquired, securing [it] is like having poured water inside an unbaked clay vessel and keeping [it].
translation: Acquiring wealth through deceitful means and trying to secure it is like trying to store water in a vessel of unbaked clay.
modern: வஞ்சக வழியால் செல்வத்தைச் சேர்த்து அதைப் பாதுகாக்க நினைப்பது, சுடப்படாத பச்சை மண் பாத்திரத்தில் நீரை ஊற்றி வைக்க முயற்சிப்பது போன்றதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet warns against using dishonest means to acquire wealth. The word 'சலம்' here refers to deceit or dishonesty, which compromises the purity of action. Trying to protect or secure ('ஏமார்த்தல்') such ill-gotten gains is compared to pouring water into a pot made of unbaked clay ('பசுமண் கலம்'). Just as the raw clay pot will dissolve and lose the water, dishonest wealth will quickly disintegrate, destroying itself and its owner.
